description: At the Saphan Nak airfield entrance from 1988 serialled 78392, repainted 2540 / FR9 in 2002 and moved into the museum by November 2010; remarked several times and carried 2021 from October 2022 through January 2026.
Probably ex US Army 59-4948. A technical training airframe outside the Maintenance Battalion until moved into the museum by January 2012.
Probably ex US Army 67-15877; airworthy at Saphan Nak until 2015 and first noted displayed inside the museum January 2023.

Composite airframe, reportedly the UH-1C brought back from Vietnam by General Kattiya Sawasdipol and displayed at the Royal Guard 1st Infantry HQ in Bangkok until about 2010, with RTAVF-111 visible under the paint. It is not UH-1B 63-8626 (destroyed in Vietnam 1965) and the panel radio call 70-16375 belongs to another aircraft; pitot positions suggest a UH-1C/M/E front end mated to a UH-1H tail.
Ex US 79-23403, c/n 16042 from the data plate. In the museum since January 2017.
Ex US 79-23412, c/n 16051 from the data plate. Cabin pod only, displayed inside the museum since January 2012.
Ex US 79-23415. In the museum since January 2012.
Ex US 79-23409, c/n 16048. A technical training airframe marked 3409 in 2005, in the museum marked 6048 from 2012 and remarked 5048 by January 2023.
New to the museum between January 2023 and January 2026.
Ex US Army 64-13148. In the museum area since 1995; marked variously 3148 and 4563 but carried 413148 again from January 2024 through January 2026.
Ex US 50-1601, c/n 21295 from the data plate. At Lopburi since November 1995.
Probably ex US 51-12499. Suspended from the museum roof since January 2012.
Possibly ex US 51-4768. In the museum since January 2012.

Ex US 51-5026, c/n 21930 from the data plate; a derelict fuselage at the Lopburi Maintenance Battalion in 2001, then with Tango at Amphur Khaeng Koi and Saraburi Aero Park. In the museum marked 5026 from 2012 and repainted 5020 by January 2020, which is not its true serial.

c/n 22129 from the data plate, therefore really ex US 51-7390; displayed marked 7350. Ex Lopburi Maintenance Battalion via Tango Amphur Khaeng Koi and Saraburi Aero Park; in the museum since January 2012.

c/n 547 from the data plate. Displayed at Lopburi marked 16151 from 1995 and remarked 6151 when moved into the museum by January 2012.
aliases: U6A; Beaver; 16151; DHC-2; c/n 547; U6; DHC2

description: c/n 1270748 from the data plate. Displayed as 5404 until 2013, as 6732 from 2020 and remarked 3639 by January 2026.
Panel radio call 6735, therefore really c/n 0842 ex US 67-16735. Airworthy with Tango at Lopburi until 2007; in the museum marked 1253 since June 2012.
Probably c/n 2039; a technical training airframe marked 2039 until moved into the museum by January 2012 and remarked 3039.
Really ex Royal Thai Police 1606, c/n 2064; stored on the police apron at Don Mueang until 2010 and restored in Army markings as 0704 for the museum by January 2012.

Composite airframe of unknown identity, partly re-covered in metal; a technical training airframe marked 1348 until 2005, in the museum marked 4870 from 2012 and repainted 2689 by January 2020. It is not 45-4870.
c/n MC-22-101, ex N200LB, manufactured October 1994; exported to Thailand 25 February 2002. Suspended from the museum roof since January 2018.
